    words_string("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
    words_string("One, two, three, four, five, six") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]
    """
\nYour job is to reason through the problem step by step and then create a Python implementation that satisfies the requirements of the docstring. To help with your reasoning, you will be given a Dafny specification, but prioritize the docstring as the Dafny specification could be incorrect. user_prompt:
method words_string(s: string) returns (result: seq<string>)
    requires s != null
    ensures result != null
    ensures |result| > 0 ==> forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] != ""
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> (result[i] in s)
    ensures |result| == CountWords(s)

method CountWords(s: string) returns (count: int)
    requires s != null
    ensures count >= 0
    ensures count == |SplitWords(s)|
    
method SplitWords(s: string) returns (words: seq<string>)
    requires s != null
    ensures |words| == CountWords(s)
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |words| ==> words[i] != ""
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |words| ==> (words[i] in s)

problem_data.prompt:
def words_string(s):
    """
    You will be given a string of words separated by commas or spaces. Your task is
    to split the string into words and return an array of the words.
    
    For example:
    words_string("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
    words_string("One, two, three, four, five, six") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]
    """
problem_data.test:
def check(candidate):

    # Check some simple cases
    assert True, "This prints if this assert fails 1 (good for debugging!)"
    assert candidate("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
    assert candidate("One, two, three, four, five, six") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]
    assert candidate("Hi, my name") == ["Hi", "my", "name"]
    assert candidate("One,, two, three, four, five, six,") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]

    # Check some edge cases that are easy to work out by hand.
    assert True, "This prints if this assert fails 2 (also good for debugging!)"
    assert candidate("") == []
    assert candidate("ahmed     , gamal") == ["ahmed", "gamal"]
